overview.text: The Western (or Green) Whip Snake is a fast, slender snake of south-western Europe. It is usually counted as harmless, although it has small grooved teeth at the back of the mouth.

identification.text: Slender with a small head, big eyes with round pupils and smooth scales. Greenish-yellow with heavy dark green or black bands, especially towards the front; the tail has thin stripes. In parts of Italy and further east many are almost completely black. Young ones are greyish.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: North-eastern Spain, Andorra, France (with Corsica), southern Switzerland, Italy (with Sardinia and Elba), Malta, Slovenia and coastal Croatia.

habitat.text: Forests, shrubland, Mediterranean scrub, farmland, pastures, rural gardens and even towns.

behaviour.label: Bites
behaviour.text: A man who was bitten for several minutes had some effects on his nerves and muscles, and the snake has been found to have small rear fangs linked to a gland - so it should not be handled.

recognise.text: Yellow-green with heavy dark bands, or all black.
